# House visual style

Defaults for generated imagery in this workspace.

- Palette: muted teal (#2a6f77), warm sand (#d9c5a0), off-black (#1a1a1d), paper white (#f5f2ea). One accent per piece, never two.
- Composition: single clear subject, generous negative space, horizon or baseline in the lower third.
- Lighting: soft directional light, long shadows acceptable, no lens flare.
- Texture: subtle grain is fine; avoid plastic-smooth gradients.
- Type pairing for renderText: a geometric sans for headings, ample letter spacing, no more than two weights per image.

When a project defines its own style file, the project file wins over this one.

# Prompt templates

Reusable starting points per pipeline.

## DALL-E (limner_generate_dalle)
`<subject>, <setting>, <lighting>, <mood>, <medium>` — keep under 80 words; the model rewrites long prompts unpredictably.

## Midjourney (limner_generate_midjourney)
`<subject> :: <style reference> --ar 3:2 --stylize 250` — the tool composes the prompt string only; paste it into your Midjourney client.

## Recraft (limner_generate_recraft)
Lead with the style id when one is set, then subject and constraints. Vector styles respond well to flat shape language: 'flat shapes, limited palette, no gradients'.

# Pipeline notes

Observations that hold across projects.

- DALL-E: sizes 1024x1024, 1536x1024, 1024x1536. Square is the safest default; wide crops lose edge detail.
- Recraft: raster styles for scenes, vector styles for icons and badges. Vector output upscales cleanly; raster does not.
- Midjourney: prompt-only pipeline, human in the loop. Record the final upscaled seed in project notes so a series can be extended later.
- General: generate at the largest size the provider offers, then downscale with compose resize. Upscaling after the fact always loses.

# Compose recipes

Op chains that come up repeatedly (limner_compose).

## Web-ready hero
resize (width 1600) -> sharpen (mild) -> convert to webp quality 82. Good size-to-quality balance for page headers.

## Thumbnail strip
crop to square on the subject -> resize 320x320 -> convert to webp quality 75.

## Watermarked preview
resize (width 800) -> watermark (corner placement, low opacity overlay) -> convert to jpeg quality 70. Use for shareable drafts; keep the clean master separate.

## Text card
renderText (heading on transparent ground) -> watermark onto a generated background -> encode png. Render text last when crispness matters; raster scaling softens glyph edges.

# Aurora Postcards — brief

A four-piece postcard series of northern-lights landscapes, one per season. Demo project used to exercise the full generate -> compose -> record loop.

Deliverables: four 1536x1024 masters plus web previews at 800 wide.

Constraints:
- Same vantage point in all four pieces; the season changes, the framing does not.
- Aurora colors stay within the house palette's teal family; snow and foliage carry the seasonal cues.
- No people, no buildings, one gnarled pine on the right third for scale.

Status tracking lives in progress.md; palette and lighting decisions in style.md.

# Aurora Postcards — style

Project overrides on top of the global house style.

- Palette: aurora bands in teal-to-green only (#2a6f77 to #4f9d6b). Sky base near-black with a cold blue cast. Snow takes the warm sand tint at the horizon.
- Composition: identical framing across the series. Horizon at the lower quarter, pine anchored at the right third, aurora arc entering from the upper left.
- Season cues: winter full snow, spring patchy melt with dark ground, summer low midnight sun glow at the horizon, autumn rust ground cover.
- Output: generate at 1536x1024, archive the master untouched, derive previews with the web-ready hero recipe.

# Aurora Postcards — progress

- Winter: master generated and accepted on the second attempt. First attempt put the pine on the left third; reinforcing the framing constraint in the prompt fixed it.
- Spring: prompt drafted, not yet generated.
- Summer and autumn: not started.

Notes for the next session: keep the accepted winter prompt as the template and vary only the season clause. The series framing constraint reads best as its own sentence, not folded into the subject clause.
